issues.text: E2S-01 (tools/test/e2e-stand.test.js) is red after sub-steps 1 and 2, as design section 12 row 1 and section 14 say. Failing line tools/test/e2e-stand.test.js:471:16, assert.deepEqual(stand.stateDirs, []): 'Expected values to be strictly deep-equal: undefined !== []'. Cause: design 4.1, the Stand table (stateDirs removed; stateEnv frozen and homeDir added). New expected behaviour: section 11.1, row E2S-01 ({...stand.stateEnv} deep-equals {}, frozen; homeDir = <marker>/home, mode 0700, empty while running; the folder count 0 after stop()). Fixed by TEST-DESIGNER at sub-step 3.

E2S-03 is red after sub-steps 1 and 2, as section 12 row 3 says. Failing line tools/test/e2e-stand.test.js:677:9 (assertKitError, line 252:10): 'the home folder: startStand: stateDirs is replaced by stateEnv, pairs of a variable and a folder' - actual 'USAGE', expected 'PATH_REFUSED'. Cause: design 4.1, row stateDirs (refused with USAGE). The test stops at its first case; its refused cases go to countingSpawn(refusingSpawn), and its later start with the real spawn is never reached (and would be USAGE too, with no spawn). New expected behaviour: section 11.1, row E2S-03 (the cases as stateEnv, env, --dir and --dir=, the root in five spellings, opt=<home>, a script outside; accepted values given as real paths).

E2S-05 is red after sub-steps 1 and 2, as section 12 row 4 says. Failing line tools/test/e2e-stand.test.js:822:14, assert.deepEqual(counter.calls[0].options.env, expected): the actual env has in addition HOME and USERPROFILE, both the private home under the temporary root of the file. Cause: design 4.1, order step 4 (HOME and USERPROFILE given last). New expected behaviour: section 11.1, row E2S-05 (the parent's HOME set to a decoy of the test; the child's HOME, USERPROFILE and the home of its env event equal stand.homeDir).

Precision of rule P, step 3 (not a change of behaviour): checkedPath passes the REAL path returned by step 1 to assertOutsideRepo, so the three steps judge exactly the value the child gets (as the prototype does). So the refusal 'inside the repository' names the real path; for a value spelled with a link or '..' that differs from the spelling. Steps 1 and 2 name the value as given (for the form <name>=<path>, the part after '='). If the reason should name the spelling, it is one line; TEST-DESIGNER should not assert the spelling in that message for a value with a link.

The exemption of the first argument decides 'inside the repository' with assertOutsideRepo of guards.js (the same test as step 3, links followed segment by segment, also for a path that does not exist, as the designer's E2S-22 needs: its script <copy>/tools/x.js does not exist) and recognises that refusal by its reason (the message ends with ': inside the repository'); any other refusal (a path that cannot be used) is thrown as it is. guards.js has no exported 'is inside' and is outside the write set. Named for REVIEWER.

Limits of rule P as the design writes it, recorded, not changed: only the part after the FIRST '=' is looked at, so a value like a=b=<absolute path> is not a path for the rule; a relative value is never a path (F12); cwd is not checked (4.1). The order of the USAGE checks is not fixed by the design: the old key stateDirs is refused first ('stateDirs' in options, own or inherited, so also stateDirs: undefined), then the other options in the order they had.

The stand-in's guard compares the REAL path of its home (fs.realpathSync(os.homedir())) with the real temporary root, and writes into that real path; the file is made with the flag 'wx' (a new file only, not through a link). So a link inside the temporary root that points to the person's home is refused too. A write that fails prints 'fake stand: the home folder was not written: <code>' to stderr and logs no event (4.2 names no failure event); a test that waits for home-written then fails on its own limit.

A slip of mine, reported in full: to count the modes I ran from tools/ the command node -e with an import of test/fixtures/e2e-stand/fake-stand.js.
